title: RunRequest
description: The single argument to Runner.run(). Five fields, each answering a question the control plane must not leave to the runner: who is asking (principal), what persona answers (profile), what is being asked (task), what it may touch (workspace), and what it may spend (budget).

contract_version.description: The contract revision this request is written against. A runner that does not recognise the value must refuse the run rather than guess.

run_id.description: Control-plane-assigned identifier, unique per run. Every event the run emits repeats it, so events from concurrent runs can share a transport.

principal.description: Who the run acts for. Never inferred by the runner from the task text.

subject.description: Stable identifier of the requesting human or system, opaque to the runner.

issuer.description: Which authority vouched for the subject: a chat platform, an OIDC issuer, or 'system' for control-plane-initiated runs.

display_name.description: Human-readable name, for prose only. Never an authorization input.

attributes.description: Issuer-specific claims the tool plane may consult (groups, tenant). Opaque to the runner, which must forward rather than interpret them.

profile.description: Which persona answers. A reference, not the persona itself: the runner resolves it, so profile content is never on the wire.

revision.description: Pins a specific version of the profile. Omitted means whatever the runner currently has, which is only acceptable for interactive runs.

input.description: The instruction text. Maps to the 'input' field of a /v1/responses request.

conversation.description: Opaque prior-context handle. Two requests carrying the same value continue one conversation; omitted means a fresh one. The control plane owns the value, so a runner may not invent one.

attachments.description: Workspace-relative paths the task refers to. Paths, never bytes.

workspace.description: What the run may touch on disk.

mode.description: 'none' denies filesystem work outright; 'read-only' permits reads; 'read-write' permits writes inside path and nowhere else.

path.description: Absolute path of the run's private tree. Required unless mode is 'none'; a runner must reject a request that omits it otherwise.

lease.description: Identifier of the lease that granted the path, for the reaper to match against. See docs/designs/gitops-workspace-leases.md.

budget.description: What the run may spend. An empty object means the control plane set no ceiling, which a runner may still refuse.

max_tokens.description: Total model tokens across the run, input and output.

deadline_seconds.description: Wall-clock ceiling measured from the first event.
